name: PJSA104_Hosho
description: Japan started its first experiments with aircraft carriers with a continuous flight deck right after World War I. They decided to convert a navy tanker that had been laid down in 1919 into an aircraft carrier. Hōshō entered service in December 1922. She was initially used to test the capabilities of carrier-based aircraft, but she then took part in the Shanghai incident and also played a role in the Sino-Japanese War in 1937. Later, she was transferred to the Combined Fleet and carried out reconnaissance and anti-submarine defense missions for the fleet's main forces.

consumables.name: Damage Control Party
consumables.description:
Extinguishes fires, removes instances of flooding, and repairs damaged modules.
Prevents enemy submarine-launched torpedoes from homing.

consumables.name: Interceptors
consumables.description:
Follow the ship and automatically attack enemy aircraft.

Can attack Airstrike squadrons multiple times before returning to the ship.

Invulnerable against hostile fighters, do not attack them, and cannot spot enemy ships.
